# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

<!-- cap-evolve:framework-improvements-append-below -->

## Iteration cand_0001
- The single most decisive fact for editing well — that `reward_basis = [DB, COMMUNICATE]` and ACTION checks are OFF — is buried in the tau2 evaluator source, not in INSTRUCTIONS.md. Every optimizer will independently rediscover it (or waste an iteration optimizing action-arg exactness that can't move reward). Suggest INSTRUCTIONS.md surface the ACTIVE reward_basis for the task up front. This is capability-agnostic: any graded-rubric task should state which rubric terms actually multiply into the score.
- The gate appears 1-shot per candidate, but a candidate can bundle N independent edits; val alone can't attribute Δ to a specific edit. The framework already stamps broke/fixed task sets (great) — recommend making that attribution guidance explicit in the JOURNAL template ("if you bundle edits, rely on broke/fixed not val to attribute"), so optimizers design bundles they can actually learn from.
- A read-only "does my tool file still parse + expose exactly one top-level function" linter hook would catch the phantom-tool footgun before scoring, turning a silently-voided measurement into an immediate, fixable error.
